title: Fix/scripture width field sizing
summary: In **Settings** → **Display & Theme**, the **Scripture Width** number used to be cut off once it reached 100 or more, so you'd see something like `16` instead of `168`. The number box is now wide enough for three digits and the number is centered in it. Nothing else about the setting changed.

links.label: Issue 2120: Scripture width gets cutoff when value is 100 or more.

setup.title: Open the preview on a computer
setup.body: Use Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari on a laptop or desktop, with the browser window wide (full screen is best). The **Scripture Width** control is hidden on phone-sized screens. Open the preview build with the button above. If it shows an error or doesn't load, the build may still be deploying: wait a few minutes and reload.

setup.title: Make sure you have the new version
setup.body: The app saves a copy of itself, so you may see the old version at first. Do a hard refresh: **Ctrl+Shift+R** on Windows, or **Cmd+Shift+R** on Mac. A private/incognito window also gives you a clean start. You don't need to sign in.

setup.title: Find Scripture Width
setup.body: Open **Settings** (the gear icon), then choose **Display & Theme**. Scroll down to the row labeled **Scripture Width**: it has a **−** button, a number followed by `ch`, and a **+** button. All tests start here.

setup.title: Optional: try a second browser
setup.body: Browsers draw numbers slightly differently. If you can, repeat the first section in a second browser (for example Firefox or Safari if you started in Chrome).

sections.title: Three-digit widths show in full
sections.intro: This is the bug from the issue: values of 100 or more were cut off.

tests.title: A width over 100 shows all three digits
tests.why: The exact problem reported in the issue.
tests.before: The number shows a two-digit value, such as `68` (the starting value for a fresh browser). If yours shows something else, that's fine; just make sure it's two digits.
steps: Click in the number box, just to the **left** of the first digit (press **Home** on Windows, or **Cmd+Left arrow** on Mac, to be sure the cursor is at the start).
Click somewhere empty on the page so the box loses focus.
expected: The box shows all three digits (for example `168`), with nothing cut off on either side.
`ch` follows right after the number, and the number sits centered between the **−** and **+** buttons.
The Bible text on the page becomes wider.

tests.title: The widest value, 192, shows in full
tests.why: 192 is the largest allowed value, and `9` is one of the widest digits.
steps: Click in the number box just to the left of the first digit, as before.
Type `2` (for example `168` becomes `2168`, which is above the maximum).
Click somewhere empty on the page.
expected: The box shows `192` in full, with no digit cut off.

tests.title: Stepping across 100 with the buttons looks right on both sides
tests.why: Checks the number keeps fitting as it changes between two and three digits.
steps: Click in the number box and hold the **Down arrow** key until the number drops below 100, then release it.
Click **−** once, so it shows `99`, then **+** once more.
expected: `99` and `100` both show in full and are centered in the box.
The row doesn't jump around or shift the **−** and **+** buttons as the number goes from two to three digits.

sections.title: Things that should not have changed

tests.title: Two-digit widths still look normal
tests.why: The number used to be right-aligned and is now centered. A two-digit value shouldn't look oddly placed.
steps: Hold the **Down arrow** key in the number box until it stops at the smallest value, `24`.
Look at the number, then click **+** a few times.
expected: The number stops at `24` and doesn't go lower.
Two-digit numbers are fully visible and centered, with `ch` right after them, and don't look like they have a big gap on one side.
The Bible text gets narrower as the number goes down and wider as it goes up.

tests.title: The number is readable in dark mode
steps: On the same **Display & Theme** page, switch to a dark theme.
Set **Scripture Width** to a three-digit value such as `150` (use the steps from the first test).
expected: The number is light text on a dark background, easy to read, and shows all three digits.

tests.title: The width you chose is kept after a reload
steps: Set **Scripture Width** to a three-digit value, for example `168`.
Reload the page, then go back to **Settings** → **Display & Theme**.
expected: **Scripture Width** still shows the value you set, in full, and the Bible text is still that wide.

notCovered: Typing a brand-new three-digit number by first selecting the whole field and typing over it can be awkward, because the box applies each digit as you type it and a single digit is below the minimum of `24`. That behavior isn't part of this change, so the tests above add a digit in front instead.
Phone-sized screens: the Scripture Width control isn't shown there, and this change doesn't affect that.
